4ee5ad4681da89a7.title: NSEL releases ₹1,950 cr in one-time settlement, ends 14-yr payment default
4ee5ad4681da89a7.summary: The National Spot Exchange Ltd (NSEL) on Monday said it has released a one-time settlement (OTS) payout of Rs 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, bringing closure to the Rs 5,600 crore payment default crisis after nearly 14 years of legal battle. The Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) had approved the settlement scheme. The full amount was deposited in a settlement account, with payouts to eligible specified creditors scheduled for November 23, 2026. The money was paid to 63 Moons Technologies, which acted as assignee of the specified creditors. On October 8, a special court in Mumbai allowed the monetisation of assets worth about Rs 3,464 crore that were attached by the Enforcement Directorate, to help fund the settlement. The scheme was first proposed by the NSEL Investors Forum, an association representing a large number of traders. NSEL, backed by 63 Moons Technologies, accepted the proposal and filed it before the tribunal as a full and final settlement.

He had assumed charge as the chief secretary in September 2025. IAS Sampath Kumar has emerged as the frontrunner for the post of Chief Secretary to the Government of Meghalaya. Born in May 1970, Kumar is a 1997-batch IAS officer in the Assam-Meghalaya cadre. He holds a Bachelor of Engineering degree (Electronic and Communications Engineering) from Osmania University. He also earned a Master of Public Administration from Harvard Kennedy School, according to his LinkedIn profile. Kumar is currently serving as Additional Chief Secretary in the Meghalaya government, according to the Government of Meghalaya's website. However, his LinkedIn profile says, "I am currently designated as the Principal Secretary & Development Commissioner, Government of Meghalaya, India (Depts of Health & Family Welfare; Women & Child Development; Community & Rural Development and Programme Implementation & Evaluation Dept)." He oversees several significant portfolios, including Community and Rural Development, Social Welfare, and Health and Family Welfare. e2017abf5e24f72e.title: Fifty years ago | Round-the-clock milk supply in Bombay
e2017abf5e24f72e.summary: Published - November 24, 2026 04:50 am IST Bombay, November 23: With Bombay all set for a “milk flood” the citizens will now be able to get “milk round-the-clock” and at their doorstep also. This facility will be made available from co-operative institutions and private agencies who have been invited by the Government to take delivery of milk for distribution. Agencies with sufficient refrigeration facilities will be entrusted with the task. Mr. S. A. Solankhe, Maharashtra Minister for Dairy Development, told pressmen here on Monday that availability of milk for Bombay had risen substantially with distribution itself increasing from 6.5-lakh litres a day in November last eight-lakh litres to-day. 74ceeeb6ce83d7eb.title: Japan’s Real Baby Bump Is All Relative
74ceeeb6ce83d7eb.summary: Did Japan just experience its first baby bump in a decade? For years, it has been the poster child for low fertility, with births falling every year since 2015. But in the first six months of 2026, there was an unexpected uptick: Births of Japanese nationals rose 0.4%, or 1,379 more than in the same period in 2025. Some supporters of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi were quick to claim this as more evidence that she’s restoring the country to its former glory; others noted that, since she took office only in October 2025, all these babies were conceived under her predecessor. Coming in the year of the hinoe uma, the Fire Horse of the Chinese zodiac, it seems impressive. The last such year, 1966, put a massive dent in births thanks to a bygone superstition that girls born in the year of the Fire Horse made poor wives . But it’s certainly no sea change. In fact, the blip might be over. Births in Japan are closely linked to marriages and those are down again this year after rising for the past two years in a rebound from Covid, which suppressed encounters of all kinds. The increase is also tiny next to the more than 14% jump in births next door in South Korea. However, there is a win hiding in plain sight in Japan’s data. As the earliest industrialized country to suffer falling births, Japan remains synonymous with the problem worldwide. But in recent years almost all of the developed world has followed, including several of its neighbors, where the decline has been faster and steeper. As a result, Japan is now the surprising outlier among East Asia’s richest economies. It has the highest fertility rate of the group, at 1.14. All of its peers have fallen below 1. A rate of around 2.1 is needed to hold population levels steady. For years, many assumed that Japan’s low figure was the floor. Now the obvious question is what kept the fertility rate from tumbling below one — and are there lessons for the world in what looks like, if not success, then at least a lesser degree o

71f0dc9f4e454c14.title: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu
71f0dc9f4e454c14.summary: Updated - November 24, 2026 02:04 am IST Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran called on Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj recently. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission (SLDHC) in Chennai is proposing to strengthen cooperation in medical education in Tamil Nadu, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students. Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran met Health Minister K.G. Arunraj in this regard recently. “During the meeting, discussion focused on further strengthening cooperation in the field of medical education, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical studies in Tamil Nadu under a proposed 50/50 scholarship between the government of Tamil Nadu and the university concerned,” SLDHC said in a social media post. Mr. Geathiswaran meeting with the Minister last week also explored the potential for establishing student exchange programmes for medical students and postgraduate trainees, including opportunities for clinical rotations, academic exchanges and professional engagement between medical institutions in Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu, it said. a9e4215c6f206f07.title: A hundred years ago | India’s military problem
a9e4215c6f206f07.summary: Published - November 24, 2026 04:40 am IST London, November 23: Referring to the recent tank demonstration at Camberley, a contributor to The Daily Telegraph declares that the Imperial effect of this object lesson was the most important. So long as India clings stubbornly to the belief in the effectiveness of scattered forces of the infantry so long must the War Office maintain proportionate infantry battalions at home and India’s refusal to utilise artillery tractors involves expensive training of gunners in modern methods at home which they must unlearn when faced with horsedrawn teams in India. The contributor suggests that a force invading India would find the easiest entry through Baluchistan and lays stress on the utility of tanks and armoured cars for the defence of North-west Frontier and maintaining order in cases of mob violence. He urges India to reconsider her military problem with a view to utilising modern mechanicalised forces. The Initial Public Offering (IPO) will close on November 30, while bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 25, according to the public announcement on Monday. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to Rs 192 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 88,35,382 equity shares worth Rs 168.76 crore by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the price band, the total issue size works out to Rs 360.76 crore. The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets, as per the RHP (Red Herring Prospectus). A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services ...

10461aa8358e6483.title: Residents urge PM, President to intervene over Pallikaranai wetland restrictions
10461aa8358e6483.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:06 am IST - Chennai Residents of Pallikaranai, Madipakkam, Velachery, Perungudi, Thoraipakkam, Sholinganallur, Karapakkam, and Perumbakkam have sought the intervention of the President and Prime Minister to safeguard their property rights, following the Madras High Court judgment dated November 18, 2026 , imposing a 1-km construction restriction around Pallikaranai Marshland. In a representation dated November 19, the Residents’ Welfare Associations of the affected areas said the restriction had caused uncertainty among thousands of families who had been living in these localities for several decades. The representation, submitted by social activist S.M. Govindarajan, representing the associations , said several families had acquired the properties through registered transactions, possessed sale deeds and patta documents, obtained building approvals, and invested their lifetime savings in their homes. They were now facing uncertainty over property rights, construction permissions, and bank loans. While expressing support for the conservation of Pallikaranai Marshland, a Ramsar site, the associations said genuine encroachments into the wetland should be distinguished from legally owned properties in established residential areas. They sought an independent scientific survey and ground-level demarcation to distinguish the marshland, drainage channels, and ecologically sensitive areas from residential properties. They also urged the authorities to examine the Tamil Nadu State Wetland Authority’s revised interim proposal to declare 36 survey numbers, covering 128.19 hectares, as a Zone of Influence, subject to scientific verification and Supreme Court directions. The representation also sought interim relief permitting essential repairs and maintenance, wherever environmentally permissible, an opportunity for affected residents to present their grievances before the Supreme Court, and a time-bound policy on properties within the restrict

The bank had initially estimated an ECL provision requirement of Rs 9,000-10,000 crore based on preliminary manual calculations. bcfecc28ef7b5575.title: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
bcfecc28ef7b5575.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there. Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008. In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers. "The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters. He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland

In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers. "The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters. He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland

2989b59d8978306f.title: Oil, gas import bill up 60% in Oct as Brent surges, LPG use declines
2989b59d8978306f.summary: India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60 per cent year-on-year to USD 16 billion in October as Brent crude averaged USD 124.77 a barrel, almost double that of a year earlier, according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), part of the oil ministry. The net bill was USD 10.0 billion in October 2025. Crude imports alone cost USD 19.5 billion, against USD 10.4 billion a year ago, even though volumes rose only 11 per cent to 23.3 million tonnes. LNG imports cost USD 1.3 billion, and petroleum product exports brought in USD 6.3 billion. Brent averaged USD 116.77 in September and USD 64.75 in October 2025. The Indian basket averaged USD 119.91 in October, against USD 65.08 a year earlier. Over April-October, the net import bill reached USD 97.7 billion, up from USD 70.3 billion a year earlier. Crude imports rose 2.7 per cent in volume but cost USD 111.0 billion, against USD 72.3 billion. Consumption of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fell 12.3 per cent in October

6a7f60d30811e66d.title: A hundred years ago | Plea for gold currency
6a7f60d30811e66d.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 04:40 am IST Delhi, November 22: The Hon. Mr. Manmohandas Ramjee, member of the Council of State, has explained his views on the proposals for currency reform in his letter to the Bombay Government on the draft Currency Bill published by the Government of India. He is in favour of 1s. 6d. ratio, but puts forward a strong plea for the early introduction of a gold currency without which public opinion in India would not be satisfied. The 1s. 6d. ratio, he says, has been working for at least two years pretty fairly and the substitution of any other ratio at this stage would mean the unsettling of business conditions and giving firms a set-back to whatever recovery it has been possible to effect in the world of trade and industries. He does not agree with the arguement that the adjustment of prices has not taken place and that, therefore, the substitution of 1s 4d. would not lead to any unsettled conditions. He believes with the Royal Commission that adjustment of prices has taken place and that therefore, any substitution now would lead to a great deal of unfairness and injustice against particular sections of business world and also, against a large body of consumers. 125c9d47652dfff4.title: Shree Cement to cross 100 MT capacity in 3-4 yrs, targets 9-10% growth
125c9d47652dfff4.summary: Shree Cement, the country's third-largest cement maker by installed capacity, is expecting to cross the 100 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) production capacity over the next three to four years, driven by an aggressive expansion push and steady demand from the country's infrastructure and housing sectors, said its Chairman Hari Mohan Bangur. In an interaction with PTI, Bangur said the company is targeting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9-10 per cent over the next six to seven years, higher than the expected 7-8 per cent growth in the overall Indian cement industry. Shree Cement Ltd (SCL), which earlier this month announced a Rs 7,000 crore investment to set up cement plants in Andhra Pradesh as part of its expansion, expects to reach 80 MTPA capacity in the next two years, he said. In response to a question on whether Shree Cement would cross 100 MTPA, Bangur told PTI: "Yes, in the next 3-4 years." SCL is having a combined investment of nearly Rs 3,500 crore to Rs 4,000 cr

f44232bb1a76c36b.title: Walkathon stresses importance of natural childbirth
f44232bb1a76c36b.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:11 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Nursing college students participate in a walk to promote natural birthing during a programme organised by the Society of Midwives India (SOMI) in Vijayawada, on Sunday. | Photo Credit: G. N. Rao Ensuring that childbirth is safe, dignified and empowering for a mother is a collective responsibility, said Andhra Pradesh Transport Department Employees Association, Zone-II, president M. Rajubabu. Inaugurating a walkathon, organised in response to a call by the Society of Midwives India to promote awareness of natural childbirth, in Vijayawada on Sunday, November 22, Mr. Rajubabu emphasised the importance of maternal health, proper nutrition, regular antenatal check-ups and family support. He highlighted that emotional well-being, confidence and a supportive family environment are as important as medical care during pregnancy. He described the walkathon as more than a fitness activity, calling it a movement for maternal health, safe childbirth, women’s dignity and healthier future generations. He urged students and youth to spread awareness in every community. Government Nursing College principal S. Naga Seshamma said that the initiative aimed to promote natural childbirth, reduce medically unnecessary caesarean deliveries and highlighted the vital role of trained midwives. She stressed that caesarean sections must be respected wherever medically necessary, with delivery decisions guided by the health and safety of mother and baby. Students from the Government Nursing College, Pinnamaneni Siddhartha Nursing College and BC and SC hostels enthusiastically participated. Faculty members, association representatives and women’s organisations also attended. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan here, Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else.

9dec6eb2521e9bc5.title: ITC extends Braille-enabled packaging to Fiama, takes total to 16 SKUs
9dec6eb2521e9bc5.summary: Alongside an industry-wide shift toward AI-enabled personalisation and algorithmic optimisation, diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd is pursuing an analogue, inclusive approach to product innovation by incorporating raised Braille text on select personal care items from its Savlon and Fiama portfolios. The initiative makes everyday consumer products more accessible to millions of visually impaired people in India, for whom routine activities such as identifying a handwash bottle or choosing the right personal care product can pose challenges. Building on Savlon's introduction of India's first Braille-enabled FMCG packaging in 2018, ITC's Personal Care Products Business has now extended the initiative to Fiama. It now has 16 SKUs from the personal care segment under accessible packaging. Braille identifiers are currently featured on technically feasible product packs, such as Savlon Antiseptic Disinfectant Liquid, Savlon Wet Wipes and Handwash Pumps, as well as Fiama Shower Gels. ITC .

b0a53c1cd2b3b729.title: Who is Cliff Savage? 36-year-old streamer lands ₹1.13 crore job to play GTA 6 for US startup
b0a53c1cd2b3b729.summary: US-based prediction market platform Kalshi has appointed 36-year-old streamer Cliff Savage to research the virtual economy of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). The California resident will receive more than $100,000 for playing the highly anticipated video game, analysing its in-game economy and sharing his observations with audiences. Savage was selected from a pool of more than 33,000 applicants who applied for the unusual position. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour announced the appointment on X, saying Savage's application “stood out the most”. Explaining why the company selected him, Mansour shared details of Savage's career journey. “He started his career as a SoundCloud artist, then discovered streaming and moved to Twitch. He hustled for a while, averaging 30 viewers per stream,” Mansour wrote. The job advertisement had offered a base salary of $100,000-$120,000 (approximately ₹ 1.13 crore) for the contract period, along with an additional $15,000 allowance for gaming and streaming expenses. The selected candidate was expected to start playing GTA 6 at midnight on its release date, November 19, and spend more than 10 hours a day exploring the game. Cliff Savage is a gaming content creator from Corona, California, who previously combined livestreaming on Twitch with occasional gig economy jobs to earn a living. Despite not having a massive online following, he managed to secure the position ahead of thousands of other applicants. A Bloomberg report said Savage had just 28 viewers watching his Twitch livestream when he received the call confirming his selection. A member of the Kalshi team, who had been keeping track of his streams, informed him about the news during the broadcast. Surprised by the announcement, Savage exclaimed, “Oh my god, bro. No way, bro,” before dropping to the floor in excitement. “I got chills in my body right now.” He later described his reaction, saying, “My whole body just went numb.” Savage also expressed his ambitions for the role in a post on X

fb560893072c2f6e.title: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
fb560893072c2f6e.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:42 pm IST Javokhir Sindarov and D. Gukesh at the press conference in Geneva on Sunday. D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The colours were drawn at the opening ceremony on Sunday. The first game in the best-of-14 match will be played on Tuesday. Gukesh sounded confident going into the defence of his title, in spite of his inferior form. His rival, on the other hand, has had an exceptional year. “Compared to the last time, it feels like I am more experienced coming into the match, but whatever has happened till now just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1,” the defending champion from Chennai said. “It’s a completely different match, a completely different opponent and a different place. So I am not really thinking about other things; I just want to give my best for these 14 games.” Gukesh admitted it would be a tough test for him against Sindarov. “He has just been very consistent and in very good form,” he said. “He is surely one of the very top players who is at the very top of his game. So for sure it is going to be a real test. But I have prepared in the best way I could. I am very enthusiastic about this match, to test myself against such a strong player and to see myself what I am capable of.” Sindarov also said it would be very hard. “But I am very happy that I have got this opportunity to play for the Word championship,” he said. “There are many chess players who play all their life but do not get this chance. After winning the Candidates in Cyprus, I have been thinking about this match for the last six months, but I have been playing and a lot of travelling in that period. I will try to enjoy the match”. f7569c70ebb8177c.title: Diageo overtakes Pernod Ricard to become India's largest alco-bev firm
f7569c70ebb8177c.summary: Pernod Ricard's India revenue from operations declined 13.6 per cent in FY26 to Rs 23,701.27 crore, primarily due to the sale of its Imperial Blue business to home-grown Tilaknagar Industries, which cost the French spirits maker cede its position as India's largest alcoholic beverage player by revenue to Diageo India. Pernod Ricard India's total income, which includes other income, was at Rs 24,122.03 crore, down 12.8 per cent for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026, according to financial documents filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). With this, Pernod Ricard lost its crown of being the leading alco-beverage company by revenue to Diageo India (United Spirits Ltd), which is part of the British multinational alcoholic beverages company Diageo plc. Diageo India (United Spirits Ltd), part of British multinational alcoholic beverages major Diageo plc, a listed entity, had reported revenue from operations of Rs 27,816 crore and total consolidated income of Rs 28,294 crore

70f6c6c616dc4a11.title: India set to install additional 200 million air conditioners by 2035: IEA
70f6c6c616dc4a11.summary: India is set to install an additional 200 million air conditioners in homes over the next decade, making it the biggest driver of global energy demand growth, the International Energy Agency said in its World Energy Outlook 2026. The agency said India and Southeast Asia's share of the global stock of air conditioners (ACs) will rise from "less than 10 per cent today to 20 per cent by 2035". In India and Indonesia, the IEA said, "fewer than one in five households own an AC, despite high cooling needs". By comparison, around 90 per cent of households in Australia, Japan and the United States own at least one AC. The IEA said "for the first time in energy history", demand for cooling in buildings is overtaking demand for heating. India's electricity demand is likely to grow 6 per cent a year, over the next decade, under the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, the fastest of any major region. Total energy demand is expected to rise 2.5 per cent annually, "triple the global rate". Globally

9d4e2e73cfb7706f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:09 am IST - Chennai An 83-year-old person is battling for life after a stray cow knocked him down while he was riding a two-wheeler in Sembakkam near Tambaram on Saturday night. The Tambaram police said Loganathan was a resident of Pavananthiyar Street in Sembakkam near Tambaram. On Saturday night, he was riding his two-wheeler near his home to purchase grocery in the nearby street. As he was proceeding on his two-wheeler, a stray bull which was chasing a cow collided with his vehicle. In the impact, Loganathan fell from the vehicle and suffered a severe head injury. The locals rescued him and admitted him to a private hospital for treatment. The incident has gone viral on the social media. The Tambaram police said Loganathan was a resident of Pavananthiyar Street in Sembakkam near Tambaram. On Saturday night, he was riding his two-wheeler near his home to purchase grocery in the nearby street. As he was proceeding on his two-wheeler, a stray bull which was chasing a cow collided with his vehicle. In the impact, Loganathan fell from the vehicle and suffered a severe head injury. The locals rescued him and admitted him to a private hospital for treatment. The incident has gone viral on the social media. cf45f0e894ed982e.title: Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention
cf45f0e894ed982e.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency. The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour. The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu. Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back. A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented. “Under the Act, the Nellore Collector, should have issued notice to the boat owners, summoned them and made them pay the requisite fine. However, this has not been done.” Also, no action has been taken by the Andhra Pradesh government on the boats from Karaikal that had fished close to their coast. “The fishermen from Karaikal were the ones who had escaped along with their boats that were impounded in Andhra Pradesh,” said another source. 3498721926903552.title: WATCH | Qatari royal jet battles 65 kmph crosswinds in dramatic sideways landing in Switzerland
3498721926903552.summary: Dramatic footage of a Qatari VIP jet wrestling fierce crosswinds to land sideways at Switzerland’s Bern Airport has taken social media by storm. The 37-second clip, shared by Al Arabiya English, showed the Qatar Amiri Flight Airbus A320 visibly swaying in 65 kmph gusts before pulling off a dramatic sideways touchdown at Bern Airport. The incident reportedly occurred on Tuesday, November 17, at Belp Airport in Bern, where weather reports recorded west-south-westerly winds of 12 to 16 knots, with gusts surging up to 35 knots—roughly 65 kmph. Departing from Doha as flight QAF9, the Airbus A320-214 began its descent onto the airport’s 1,730-metre runway at around 2:40 PM local time. In the footage, the aircraft’s wings can be seen banking sharply from side to side as it descends through turbulent skies before approaching the tarmac. To counter the strong crosswinds, the pilots angled the jet’s nose into the wind—a standard aviation manoeuvre known as a “crab approach”—before straightening the aircraft moments before the landing gear touched down smoothly. According to Swiss publication 20 Minuten, aviation spotter Matthias Hänni, who filmed the descent, said he repeatedly expected the pilots to abandon the approach and climb back into the sky. Airline pilot and Swiss National Council member Thomas Hurter also told 20 Minuten that executing a go-around would have been a good option under the gusty conditions, which had reportedly forced a Swiss government aircraft to abort its own landing around the same time. As the clip—which has racked up over 4.19 lakh views on Al Arabiya English’s YouTube channel—circulated widely online, viewers speculated whether Qatar’s Emir , Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, was aboard the jet. However, Swiss media reports clarified that the Emir was not on the flight. 34e27e37c05b2507.title: Airbnb looks beyond traditional holiday hubs to deepen presence in India
34e27e37c05b2507.summary: Global hospitality platform Airbnb is looking to deepen its presence in India by expanding beyond traditional holiday destinations, strengthening the homestay ecosystem and bringing more local entrepreneurs onto its platform to tap the country's growing domestic travel market. In an interview with PTI, Airbnb India Country Manager Amanpreet Bajaj said the company's India growth strategy will focus on expanding quality accommodation supply, enabling more communities to participate in tourism and diversifying its offerings beyond stays through experiences and services. "We will also continue expanding quality supply, both in traditional leisure markets and metros and in emerging destinations such as spiritual corridors and nature-led locations. We want travellers to have more choices and local communities to benefit from tourism," Bajaj shared. He highlighted that India is one of Airbnb's fastest-growing origin markets globally, with domestic travel emerging as a major growth driver.

4d8dc7ce789bb8ae.title: Central California concert shooting: Nine people shot; one in critical condition
4d8dc7ce789bb8ae.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 04:46 am IST - Sacramento (U.S.) Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: AP Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday (November 22). In pictures: America’s deadliest mass shooting The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday (November 21) at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the centre of the state, the county sheriff's department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced. One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff's department said. Two other victims, ages 19 and 22, also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries. Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn't elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighbouring states, the department said. The department didn't immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public. e81f1b18443bc21d.title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
e81f1b18443bc21d.summary: Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said. The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said. "It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.

79e64db5f0f9b036.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have become net buyers of Indian equities, making substantial investments in November. They have invested over ₹1.18 lakh crore so far, indicating a strong market reversal. Previously, FPIs were net sellers, offloading equities worth around ₹5.51 lakh crore from October 2024 to mid-October 2026. The recent buying trend has occurred over 13 consecutive trading sessions, averaging around ₹1,450 crore per hour.

ddce85be0556323f.title: CMC honours essay, painting, quiz competition winners in Vellore
ddce85be0556323f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:00 am IST - VELLORE CMC organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers. To mark World Diabetes Day 2026, the Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMC), Vellore, organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers in Vellore. According to a press release, participants have to write an essay on “From classroom to community – Children leading the fight against diabetes”. Painting competition was “From screen time to Green time – keep diabetes away”. Quiz competition for teachers was related to general knowledge and non-communicable diseases. Around 185 students participated in various competitions at the event. Winners of the painting competition are Shavitha, Government Higher Secondary School in Poigai (Vellore), Siddharth of Shristi School (Vellore) and Ashwanth, IDA Scudder school, won first, second and third prizes respectively. In the teachers quiz competition, Savitha and Sreeja of Sunbeam CBSE School. Muthanara. and Anushya - Spark School, Savitha and Monisha of Shrishti Vidyashram School won first, second and third prizes respectively, the release said. 343b2473a205448f.title: Elderly couple found dead in Purasawalkam
343b2473a205448f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai An elderly couple was found dead in a decomposed state in Purasawalkam on Sunday. The police said Dhanraj, 78, and his wife Chandra, 72, were residents of Saravana Perumal Koil Street in Purasawalkam and the couple had no children . Dhanraj, who once ran a small jewellery workshop, had retired due to old age and the couple was living peacefully. On Sunday morning, a conservancy worker cleaning the street noticed a foul odour emanating from the house. As the couple had not been seen over the past few days, the worker alerted Kilpauk police. The police found the bodies in a decomposed state and sent them to the Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem. The police have registered a case. e7ce13627d5ffd48.title: States can now appraise non-coal mining projects spread over 500 hectares
e7ce13627d5ffd48.summary: Non-coal mining projects spread up to 500 hectares (ha) will now be appraised for environmental clearance at the state level. This threshold was 250 hectares earlier. In a notification dated November 18, the Union Environment Ministry said that the amendment would help further decentralise the environment clearance process for such projects. It also noted that state-level bodies -- State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAA) and State Expert Appraisal Committees (SEAC) -- already examine coal mining projects of up to 500 ha. While the SEIAA grants environmental clearances, the SEAC advises it in appraising the project. Under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006, projects are categorised based on their size and potential impacts. Category A projects are appraised by the Centre-level Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) and Category B projects by SEIAAs and SEACs. 13989f1d6169b162.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
13989f1d6169b162.summary: Updated - November 23, 2026 01:07 am IST That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha. Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. 4ed7bcebc2ad79d2.title: CAQM asks Delhi, NCR states to set district-level pollution targets
4ed7bcebc2ad79d2.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has asked Delhi and the NCR states to prepare action plans for 2027 to tackle air pollution and include district-level action measures in them. This is the first time that the CAQM has asked governments to formulate district-level action plans, which will help facilitate focused implementation and effective monitoring of pollution control measures at the grassroots. They will also help identify implementation gaps and enable timely corrective action, with clearly defined accountability, officials said. In an order dated November 20, the CAQM said, "Dealing with air pollution requires sustained and concerted efforts based on the airshed approach. For 2027, annual action plans shall also be prepared at the district level, in addition to the state and municipal corporation levels." "The Annual Action Plan-2027 shall contain clearly defined sector-wise actions with measurable targets, timelines and monitoring .

ecd86059cc86ab8a.title: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace, 4-5 trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
ecd86059cc86ab8a.summary: Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities, according to the Bharat InvITs Association. Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. 77e41026bea2bb0f.title: MPCB asks Adani firm to stop work on temporary labour camp in Satara
77e41026bea2bb0f.summary: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to stop excavation and construction work for its temporary camp in Satara district for allegedly beginning these without obtaining the necessary environmental clearance and permissions. The labour camp in Satara's Patan taluka, some 300 kilometres from here, is part of the firm's 1500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a stop-work notice dated November 20, the MPCB said the company had started excavation and development work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawargahar village for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities without informing the board or obtaining the required permissions. The company had not secured environmental clearance for the excavation and development work from the competent authority, the MPCB added. 7c2098fd5f77e056.title: Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions
7c2098fd5f77e056.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:24 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Activists carry placards and a painting of a data centre on parched land during the rally against data centres on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. | Photo Credit: PAUL NICODEMUS Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam city. Members of Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, marched from the RK Beach bus stop to the Bhagat Singh statue, raising slogans and handing out pamphlets to passers-by. G. Kantarao, treasurer of the organisation, said the government had not said how many jobs would be created, even as data centre capacity rose to over six gigawatts. He alleged that the government was serving corporate interests by allotting hills at Rushikonda and Yendada, and those belonging to the Simhachalam Devasthanam, to private firms. He demanded that all permissions given to these corporations be cancelled. “If the government does not cancel them, we will turn this into a people’s movement,” he said. The rally ended at the Bhagat Singh statue on purpose, Mr. Kantarao said. Just as Bhagat Singh had turned the course of the freedom struggle, the organisers hoped to turn the course of this agitation. Sai Teja, district president of the Students’ Federation of India, alleged that the “Stop Vizag Data Centre” social media account had been taken down three times, most recently two days before the rally. “Why is the government so afraid?” he asked. He said development should be sustainable and create jobs. Dhyuti, a research scientist and environmentalist, said the campaigners wanted clear information on health hazards, cooling methods and skilled jobs. Visakhapatnam was prone to drought and could not spare water and land for data centres, she said. Green Visakha secretary M. Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part. Published

be6caf1bfca67d9e.title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
be6caf1bfca67d9e.summary: India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday. The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The ten-day talks concluded on November 20. "Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.

The decision was taken unanimously by all 25 directors due to the drought situation and the difficulties faced by farmers, Patil, a former MLA, said. The union has also decided to raise the procurement rates paid to milk producers by Rs 3 per litre for buffalo milk and Rs 2 per litre for cow milk, he said, adding that this hike was "historic". "The revised rates will come into effect from November 21 and remain applicable for around 131 days, till March. The situation will be reviewed every month, and the board will take further decisions depending on the circumstances," Patil said. 1610f8d0b3d08f0a.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
1610f8d0b3d08f0a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday. Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments. He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit. The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance. Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said. He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet. After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent. The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. RAGHUNATHAN While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi. “When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan. Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress. “Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. f178aaed7009168f.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
f178aaed7009168f.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - COIMBATORE Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives. The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors. “No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore. “We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu. The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added. While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. cde4ace93eda6db5.title: PM Modi to launch development projects worth ₹34,470 cr in Bihar's Vaishali
cde4ace93eda6db5.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to launch projects worth nearly 34,470 crore, including a six-lane bridge over the Ganga river, and address a public meeting, officials said. This would be the Prime Minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar. Elaborate security arrangements, including the suspension of vehicular movement on the national and state highways concerned for a stipulated period, have been made in Vaishali and Patna for the PM's visit, they said. The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former Bihar chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived and came close to completion. "The PM will visit 'Nitish Setu' in Vaishali.

"I would do it. These credit card companies have made a lot," Trump told Fox News Channel's "Saturday in America." Democrats and the Republican president have both backed capping credit card interest rates, with the standard proposal being capping rates at 10 per cent. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation (CPRAF) to mark the institution’s 60th anniversary. One of the most significant reforms associated with Sir C.P.’s term as Dewan of Travancore was the temple entry proclamation, he added. f97096ca850df3be.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
f97096ca850df3be.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:14 am IST - CHENNAI Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences. In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka. He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner. Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added. 2635f0246638e795.title: Hero FinCorp aims to double loan disbursements over next two quarters
2635f0246638e795.summary: Hero FinCorp aims to double its loan disbursement volumes over the next two quarters, after disbursing over 4.80 lakh loans across northern India between January and September this year. Financial services company Hero FinCorp Ltd is a division of two-wheeler manufacturer Hero MotoCorp. The company's growth plans will be supported by its diversified lending portfolio, distribution network and artificial intelligence-led underwriting capabilities, according to a statement. The non-banking financial company caters to diverse financing needs through a comprehensive portfolio of retail, MSME and corporate lending solutions. "Over 4.8 lakh households and businesses across seven states have chosen us this year for a two-wheeler, a car, a personal loan, working capital or a loan against property. "We aim to double our growth in the region over the next two quarters while keeping the customer's trust at the centre of every decision we make," Hero FinCorp's spokesperson said.

59a95f409159537a.title: Vijayawada girl selected for National Roller Skating Championship
59a95f409159537a.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 11:28 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Janga Harika won two silver medals at the 38th Inter-District Roller Skating Championship, held in Kakinada recently. | Photo Credit: THE HINDU Janga Harika, a Class VII student from Vijayawada, has been selected for the National-Level Roller Skating Championships after delivering an impressive performance at the 38th Inter-District Roller Skating Championship-2026. The event, organised under the aegis of the A.P. Roller Skating Association, was held on November 14 and 15 in Kakinada. Harika, who competed in the Artistic Skating category, won a silver medal in the Inline competition, another silver in the Slow Figure competition, and third place in the Solo Style Dance competition. Hailing from Vijayawada, Janga Harika is currently studying in Class VII at St. John’s Higher Secondary School, Gannavaram. Her selection for the National-Level Championships has brought immense happiness to her family, coaches, well-wishers, and sports enthusiasts. 360933fb0939b9d4.summary: Work crews were boxing up the venue of this year's United Nations climate talks in Turkiye, as negotiators went into overtime on Saturday in an attempt to reach a final agreement to address global warming. But hopes are slim that additional discussions will result in concrete plans to drastically slash the use of fossil fuels. The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, called COP31, which was supposed to end Friday, drew strong condemnation from activists and some countries for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement. The final document is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which is contributing to devastating heat waves, floods and other disasters. To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut emissions from the use of coal, oil and gas. f0fc613bfcb38260.title: Heller Industries sets up India's first reflow oven mfg plant in Gujarat
f0fc613bfcb38260.summary: US-based Heller Industries Inc on Friday inaugurated its first Indian manufacturing facility near Ahmedabad, becoming the first global reflow oven maker to produce the critical semiconductor and electronics assembly equipment locally in the country. Operated through its subsidiary Heller Thermal Systems Private Limited (HTS) at Gallops Industrial Park in Rajoda, the 30,000 sq ft facility has been established with the strategic and operational support of long-term Indian partner NMTronics India Pvt Ltd, a company statement said. The plant is designed with a production capacity of 40 ovens per month. HTS plans to dispatch 18 ovens in 2026, scaling up to 146 units in 2027 and 180 units in 2028, by which time one in every three ovens built at the facility will be exported to markets across the US, Europe, and Southeast Asia, the statement said. ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.title: Chennai International Book Fair 2027 to be held from January 16 to 18
ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:08 am IST - CHENNAI Rajmohan, Minister of School Education, unveiling the logo of Chennai International Book Festival 2027 at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai on Saturday. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Saturday unveiled the logo of the Chennai International Book Fair (CIBF) 2027, which is scheduled to take place from January 16 to January 18, next year, at the Chennai Trade Centre. The Minister also inaugurated the training programme for global literary agents at the Anna Centenary Library in Chennai. The upcoming CIBF will be its fifth edition, with publishers, authors, and translators from more than 110 countries expected to participate. The Publishers and Booksellers Association of Thailand (PUBAT) will participate as a special guest. At the inaugural edition of the CIBF in 2023, publishers from 23 countries participated. The number of participating countries gradually rose from 40 in 2024 to 65 in 2025 and 102 in 2026. Across these editions, 415 translation grants were awarded to 183 authors for translating 258 books into 50 languages. The training programme for global literary agents, which began on November 21, will continue until December 5. Layola Mani, Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation, and R.V. Shajeevana, Director of Public Libraries, were present at the event. 749104a1bab252f1.title: Diversion of sanctioned posts raises concerns over postal operations in Tamil Nadu
749104a1bab252f1.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI The diversion of various sanctioned supervisory and operational posts from the Tamil Nadu Postal Circle to other States by the Postal Directorate has triggered concerns over its impact on the T.N. Circle’s administrative efficiency, service delivery and employment opportunities. The redistribution was carried out as part of the nationwide restructuring and rebalancing of administrative units across the Department of Posts. The Directorate had recently issued an order on the redistribution of the posts. The order has resulted in the transfer of nearly 180 posts across eight cadres from Tamil Nadu to other postal circles, including Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and the North-East. Sources in the department said the Tamil Nadu circle has lost only a few posts in the past decade. But this time, a large share of posts, including postal assistants, multi-tasking staff, inspectors and postmen, are being redeployed. The redistribution has come under scrutiny over the absence of an adequate assessment of the workload and establishment requirements of the Tamil Nadu Circle before the posts were diverted. Tamil Nadu postal circle handles a substantial volume of postal operations. For instance, it operates nearly 3.68 crore post office savings bank accounts across the State, which is highest number in the country, sources said. Similarly, Tamil Nadu postal circle stands second in the revenue generation with Rs.1,733 crore in 2025-26 after Maharashtra. The diversion of a large number of posts would adversely affect postal operations in about 10,000 post offices across TN, sources said. bfb228e20ab5f123.title: DMRC transplanted trees without Forest Department’s approval, official tells HC
bfb228e20ab5f123.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 04:42 am IST The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) transplanted trees removed during the construction of an underground metro line at Ajmal Khan Park without obtaining prior approval from the Delhi government’s Forest Department, the Delhi High Court was informed. The submission was made in a status report filed by the Deputy Conservator of Forests (West Division), Department of Forest and Wildlife, in response to a petition alleging that large-scale construction work was being carried out in the area, damaging fully grown trees. The petition, on which the court had earlier issued notices to the authorities, is scheduled to be heard next on November 23 by Justice Jasmeet Singh. The petitioner, advocate Arpit Bhargava, submitted that the DMRC was carrying out extensive construction work on vacant land belonging to the Delhi Development Authority on Desh Bandhu Gupta Road in Karol Bagh, behind his residence, where several large trees stand. He said substantial quantities of iron and steel rods and other construction material were being cut and processed using mechanical equipment as part of the construction work, generating smoke, dust, fumes and particulate matter. In its status report, the Forest Department said officials of the West Division conducted a joint inspection of the project site at Ajmal Khan Park on October 7, when tree transplantation work was under way. The construction is part of the Inderlok-Indraprastha Corridor of the Delhi Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) Project under Phase IV. According to the report, of the 534 trees at the site, 524 were to be transplanted and 10 felled. During an inspection, it was found that around 10-15 transplanted trees were showing signs of survival and new leaf growth, and remaining trees can survive in future as transplantation is under process, the report stated. “The transplantation site had not been approved by the Forest Department before the work began,” it added. d0b2a07d0da8a186.summary: The GST Network (GSTN) has added metro rail as a new mode of transport in the e-way bill system. Currently, the facility has also been released in the "Sandbox environment" for API users to test and make necessary changes to their systems. Its roll-out in the live API environment will be announced separately, GSTN, which manages the IT backbone of Goods and Services Tax, said. The facility follows a government notification dated October 26. With this addition, the e-way bill system now has five modes of transport: Road, Rail, Air, Ship and Metro Rail. Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the e-way bill is mandatory for transiting goods valued at Rs 50,000 and above, both inter- and intra-state. 5b4808b44ac4942b.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 11:36 pm IST - Agartala The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura slated for November 27. State Election Commissioner (SEC) Pradip Chakraborty said the MHA has informed the State government of its decision on Saturday. He added that with local availability of the CAPF, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed on election duties. The deployment will remain in force even after the declaration of results on December 2. The Opposition CPI(M) and Congress have long been demanding adequate deployment of Central forces alleging that the ruling BJP is trying to turn the elections into a farce through gross irregularities and use of government machinery. They have accused the State police of failing to discharge duties neutrally. The SEC had announced a schedule to hold elections for 21 ULBs including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC). However, the Congress and CPI(M) said clamed their candidates were prevented from filing nomination papers for five civic bodies. The BJP secured victory in five ULBs unopposed and hence, the polls will technically occur in 16 areas instead of 21. With the election campaign picking up pace, Opposition parties have alleged that their supporters are facing obstacles and threats during the door-to-door campaign. The parties have also sought the attention of the authorities after spotting several masked youth taking part in an campaign procession of the BJP in Agartala on Saturday. They alleged the youth may have been brought in from outside the State. 8e8a7928fbdbf425.summary: Beijing is building nuclear weapons at a "hot and heavy" pace, President Donald Trump said, a day after he met Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin and the three countries agreed to talks on preventing nuclear proliferation. While Russia and the US lead the world by each possessing thousands of nuclear weapons, China is rapidly expanding its nuclear arsenal. In its annual review of China's military buildup, the Pentagon said China's stockpile of nuclear warheads remained in the low 600s through 2024, but the country was on track to have more than 1,000 warheads by 2030. "They'll catch us within 10 years," Trump said of China's nuclear buildup during a news conference at the White House on Friday. "They're going at it hot and heavy, but they have a lot." Trump's public remarks were his first since his controversial summit with Xi and Putin, leaders of countries long considered US rivals, in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday. b1169cb24f4db674.title: Man held in Tirupattur for killing two persons
b1169cb24f4db674.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 12:36 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspecting the spot. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A 29-year-old man was arrested by Tirupattur Taluk police on Saturday for killing two persons on the outskirts of Tirupattur town a day ago over a reportedly extra marital relationship. Police identified the arrested person as V. Sanjay Gandhi, a resident of Tiruvannamalai. The victims are E. Ranjith Kumar, 30, a resident of Tiruvannamalai, and C. Malini, 45, a resident of Tirupattur. Initial inquiry revealed that Malini married Chiranjeevi and had two children. The family was living near Tirupattur town. Malini met her school friend Sanjay Gandhi at a function a few months ago and got in touch since then. Police said Malini got acquainted with Ranjith, a cab driver, when he visited her house to meet her husband for work. Sanjay got agitated over the relationship and warned Malini of dire consequences. Police said that on Friday, when Malini and Ranjith were returning to Tirupattur in a car, Sanjay noticed them. An argument broke between them. In a fit of rage, Sanjay killed them and fled the spot. Police said a few residents noticed the duo in a pool of blood and alerted police. A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspected the spot. CCTV cameras and mobile phones were tracked. Later, the police team nabbed Sanjay in the hideout in Tirupattur. A case was registered and further probe is under way. Police said a few residents noticed the duo in a pool of blood and alerted police. A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspected the spot. CCTV cameras and mobile phones were tracked. Later, the police team nabbed Sanjay in the hideout in Tirupattur. A case was registered and further probe is under way. 22870d99b63f2f45.title: Residents demand halts for more long-distance trains at Melmaruvathur
22870d99b63f2f45.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:56 am IST - Chennai A CPI(M) leader noted that only a few express trains were stopping at the Melmaruvathur station as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for several trains after the COVID-19 lockdown. (FILE PHOTO) | Photo Credit: D. GOPALAKRISHNAN The residents in several villages situated around Melmaruvathur have requested the Southern Railway to provide a stoppage for several mail and express trains, including Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat trains, at the Melmaruvathur Railway Station. G. Purushothaman, secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) in Seyyur taluk, has petitioned the Southern Railway to add stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur. He said that only a few express trains were stopping at the station, as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for Uzhavan Express, Kamban Express, and Silambu Express after the COVID-19 lockdown As Melmaruvathur was an important spiritual town, the place has also gained commercial importance. Residents of several villages, including Seyyur, Sithamur, Lathur, and Maduranthakam, also visit Chennai for studies, work, and trade. Similarly, those travelling to the southern districts for trade and education must go to Chengalpattu or Villupuram to catch long-distance trains. The residents want long distance trains to halt at Melmaruvathur as it has become a transport hub. A senior Southern Railway official said that since the provision of additional stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur comes under the administrative purview of Zonal Headquarters, Southern Railway headquarters would have to take a decision. Regarding the extension of suburban trains beyond Chengalpattu, the railway officer said the tracks beyond Chengalpattu railway station has not been upgraded to the prescribed standards for operation of electrical multiple unit (EMU) train services. Hence the extension of EMU train services up to Melmaruvathur was operationally not feasible

Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges. The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday. "The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court," read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla. 54678118d1e8a15e.title: EPF is becoming a retirement income plan. Is it a better one?
54678118d1e8a15e.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) board in New Delhi on Thursday (November 19) approved a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) , the Labour Ministry said. Retirees can take savings in instalments, monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, instead of one lump sum. The ministry says the plan is meant to supplement pension benefits. It is voluntary and will first be open to members above 55 with over Rs 5 lakh saved. The board also eased withdrawal rules and approved in principle investing up to 3 per cent of fresh yearly inflows in alternative investment funds (AIFs), the ministry said. Table 1: What the EPFO board changed Vivek Iyer, partner and financial services risk advisory leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, says the plan addresses “a long-standing gap in India’s retirement system”. India has focused on saving for retirement, he says, but offered little help with turning those savings into income. The advisory firm’s illustration shows how it could work. A retiree at 58 with Rs 50 lakh takes Rs 40,000 a month. If the balance keeps earning 8.25 per cent, the money lasts about 24 years, to age 82. Unlike an annuity, Iyer says, the plan lets members “keep ownership and flexibility over their corpus”. If the member dies at 68, about Rs 39.6 lakh passes to the nominee, the illustration shows. Everything hinges on interest. The ministry says the remaining money will keep generating returns. Iyer says whether it keeps earning the EPF rate “is what makes the plan attractive”. Kunal Kabra, founder of Kustodian.Life, a provident fund recovery firm, says EPF interest stops three years after retirement under current rules. On Grant Thornton’s example, that would cut the 24 years to about 13, Business Standard’s calculation shows. “If the interest still stops, then this option doesn’t make any sense,” Kabra says. It is not yet clear whether the balance under the new plan escapes that rule. The ministry has not said how instalments will be taxed . It says a corres

6d2420f6b6418046.title: T.N. govt. gave no advance notice on Justice Kurian panel’s dissolution: member
6d2420f6b6418046.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:06 am IST - Chennai Retired IAS officer K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty, a member of the committee on Union-State relations, has stated that neither he nor the panel’s head, Justice Kurian Joseph, was informed prior to its dissolution. In a detailed interview with The Hindu 360 YouTube channel, Mr. Shetty revealed that the government had initially cleared the panel to continue its work. “I think it was on May 4 when a fellow member, M. Naganathan, resigned. Because of this, we were forced to seek clarity from the government on the continuation of the committee. I spoke to the Chief Secretary asking whether we should continue, and also requested him to consider not appointing a replacement for Dr. Naganathan if we were to carry on. About a week later, the then-Public Secretary, Reeta Harish Thakkar, called me and said, ‘Sir, the government has said you can continue,’ adding that no new member would be appointed. So, we continued. While all other committees constituted during the previous regime were contacted and asked to step down, nothing of that sort happened to us. Suddenly, one day, they dissolved it,” Mr. Shetty recounted. The mandate of the dissolved panel has now been handed over to the State Law Commission. Addressing the Government Order (G.O.) that cited the Kurian Committee’s status as a non-statutory body, Mr. Shetty pointed out that the Law Commission holds the exact same legal standing. “The Law Commission was created by a 1994 G.O., and ever since, it has been reconstituted through similar orders. So, the Law Commission is also an executive body — just like we were, and just like the Punchhi and Sarkaria Commissions,” he said. He also questioned the feasibility of the transfer, noting that the State Law Commission has never examined Union-State ties in its over three decades of existence. “In the last 32 years, the State Law Commission has never gone into this issue. 8d05a4e99835b13a.title: T.N. to set up Statewide online registry of voluntary donors with rare blood groups
8d05a4e99835b13a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:13 am IST - CHENNAI To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC). In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry. The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups. The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent. The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry. The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed. At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations. In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator.
