742391430617522f.title: 8th Pay Commission: Postal employees seek major changes in promotion rules, propose 1-4 years qualifying service
742391430617522f.summary: The Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) has urged the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) to overhaul promotion rules for central government employees, proposing that the minimum qualifying service for promotions be fixed between one and four years, depending on the requirements of individual cadres. In a letter dated November 20 addressed to Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, chairperson of the 8th Pay Commission, FNPO Secretary General Sivaji Vasireddy sought a comprehensive review of the existing promotion conditions specified in the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) office memorandum issued on September 20, 2022. The federation, which represents a significant section of Department of Posts employees, argued that the existing promotion framework has created prolonged career stagnation and affected the functioning of several postal offices. According to FNPO, the annexure to the DoPT memorandum prescribes widely varying qualifying service periods for promotions across different pay levels. Some promotions require employees to wait as long as 12 years. The transition from Level 6, 9 to Level 11 has the longest qualifying period of 12 years. Similarly, promotions from Level 4 to Level 6, Level 6 to Level 10 and Level 11 to Level 13 require 10 years of qualifying service. Other promotional transitions, including Level 2 to Level 4 and Level 6 to Level 9, require eight years. In contrast, several other promotions under the same framework have qualifying service requirements ranging from just one to three years, the federation pointed out. FNPO said the prolonged qualifying service requirements have adversely affected the Department of Posts, with several important positions remaining vacant for extended periods because fewer employees become eligible for promotion. The affected positions include Lower Selection Grade and Higher Selection Grade posts, supervisory positions in postal and Railway Mail Service (RMS) offices, Senior Superintendent of Post

b4d2355380c1f0e5.title: Guru Shiksha 2026 to be held in Chennai on November 27, 28
b4d2355380c1f0e5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:07 am IST - Chennai The 11th edition of Guru Shiksha 2026, a State-level inter-school and inter-collegiate socio-cultural and educational programme, will be held at the Guru Nanak College and Guru Nanak Matriculation Higher Secondary School campus in Velachery on November 27 and 28, 2026. Organised by the Guru Nanak Educational Society and hosted by its Guru Nanak Centre for Consultancy and Outreach Initiatives, this year’s theme is ‘The Gurus’ Vision, A Woman’s Flight’, inspired by the vision of the Sikh Gurus. Oratorical events in English, Tamil and Hindi, poster-making, podcasts in English and Tamil, research papers in English, Tamil and Hindi, and letter-writing to Sikh Gurus in the three languages are some of the competitons. Students will be divided into five categories: Alpha (Classes I to V), Beta (Classes VI to VIII), Gamma (Classes IX to XII), Delta (college and university students and research scholars), and Epsilon (teaching and non-teaching staff and the general public, for specified competitions). The total prize limit exceeds ₹8 lakh. Online registrations are open, and spot registrations are available at the venue. acbc826c4119dbe5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government is exploring a new site for the Hosur airport, after the site identified in Shoolagiri taluk in Krishnagiri district was rejected by the Ministry of Defence earlier this year. The new site is located near the Taneja Aerospace and Aviation Limited (TAAL) Aerodrome in Belagondapalli (about 15 km from central Hosur). Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh government has managed to get the site clearance for Kuppam airport project from the Ministry of Civil Aviation. This makes it even more difficult to obtain clearance for the initially identified site in Shoolagiri taluk (between Berigai and Bagalur), owing to airspace constraints. Earlier, the Tamil Nadu government had brought on board Bangalore International Airport Limited, which, over the past few weeks, had conducted a study on how to expand the site close to the TAAL airstrip and develop an airport for Hosur, sources said. The report was recently submitted to the government, based on which further discussions will be held on taking the project forward, and subsequently obtaining the site clearance. “First of all, the government had already tried twice to obtain approval for the Shoolagiri site from the Ministry of Defence, but it did not happen. The possibility for obtaining site clearance was very bleak, with Kuppam airport too vying for that airspace. As expected, Kuppam airport was granted site clearance. The Shoolagiri site was also facing stiff opposition to land acquisition from the residents. Keeping all this in mind, the site near TAAL is being considered now,” a source said. For the site near TAAL too, the State government must obtain approval from the Ministry of Defence, as the airspace is controlled by the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. 4eca0410d663e864.title: USFDA flags 7 likely violations in check of NATCO Pharma's Hyderabad unit
4eca0410d663e864.summary: NATCO Pharma Limited on Saturday said it has received seven observations from the US health regulator following an inspection of its manufacturing facility in Kothur, Hyderabad. The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) conducted an inspection of the company's plant during November 12-20, NATCO Pharma said in a regulatory filing. Upon conclusion of the inspection, the company received seven observations in Form 483, it added. In USFDA parlance, a Form-483 is issued to a firm's management at the conclusion of an inspection when investigators observe conditions that, in their judgment, may constitute violations of the laws. "The company believes that the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing these observations comprehensively within stipulated timelines," NATCO Pharma said.

7a1a7a181cda5ce7.title: Nikhil Gupta sentenced to over 19 years in US prison for plot to kill Khalistani separatist Pannun
7a1a7a181cda5ce7.summary: Indian national Nikhil Gupta has been sentenced to more than 19 years in prison after he admitted his role in a foiled 2023 plot to kill Khalistani separatist and US citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in of New York. Gupta was sentenced to 235 months by US District Judge Victor Marrero at a hearing in Manhattan Friday. According to a statement issued from the US Department of Justice , 55-year-old Gupta, in February 2026, pleaded guilty to three criminal charges linked to a plan to kill Pannun . Justice Marrero called the plot to kill the US citizen inside the country "an attack on United States sovereignty", according to a Bloomberg report. Gupta was taken into custody in the Czech Republic in June 2023 and subsequently extradited to the US. The case forms part of what US prosecutors described as a wider conspiracy that strained relations between India and the US, as well as Canada. American authorities alleged that Gupta was associated with a network linked to the Indian government that sought to target Sikh separatists living overseas. The allegations also included the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar , who was shot dead by masked assailants outside a Sikh temple in western Canada in June 2023. According to prosecutors, Gupta recruited a person he believed to be a contract killer to carry out the assassination of Pannun. They alleged that he acted on instructions from Vikash Yadav, an official with India's external intelligence agency. Both Gupta and Yadav were charged with murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Yadav remains outside US custody. "Today's prison sentence reflects the seriousness of Nikhil Gupta's conduct and should serve as a clear warning: the Department of Justice and its law enforcement partners will pursue and hold accountable anyone who attempts to commit violence on US soil or against US citizens," US Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a statement. 488ecaef9940c3f2.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveils India's 1st home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine
488ecaef9940c3f2.summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled the country's first indigenously developed H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu here on Friday. The vaccine has been developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal, officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said. This is the first-of-its-kind vaccine developed in India against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), they said. Speaking on the occasion, Chouhan said, "This vaccine is an example of India's self-reliance." HPAI, commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting chickens and other birds. Outbreaks can result in almost 100 per cent mortality among infected birds. Besides the Union Agriculture Minister, Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare and Cooperatives Minister Vishwas Sarang and Bhopal BJP MP Alok Sharma, among others, were also present at the ceremony held here.

8854a402fa731af5.title: Inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 held
8854a402fa731af5.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - CHENNAI Dignitaries at the inauguration of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 in Mylapore on Friday. | Photo Credit: V. UMESH KUMAR Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan touches the lives of millions of people directly, N. Ravi, Chairman of Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra and Director of Kasturi and Sons Limited, said on Friday. At the inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026, organised in association with South Zone Cultural Centre, Mr. Ravi said the institution has a vast national and global footprint retaining its original vision, ideals, and values. Bhavan’s activities encompass culture in its widest sense and are carried out through its kendras . “This Margazhi season, there are over 2,000 music and dance performances in the city, making it one of the largest music festivals in the world. In tune with this character of the city, the Chennai Kendra has organised this festival as its flagship event. For the next 45 days, we will be featuring over 1,000 artists in the main and supporting roles,” he added. B.K. Krishnaraj Vanavarayar, Vice-President, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, said, “There is something each country will be proud of. As far as India is concerned, our culture is our pride and it is rooted in spirituality. All the great acharyas, political leaders, and great men have visited the Bhavan’s various branches.” K.K. Gopalakrishnan, Director, South Zone Cultural Centre, said he was glad they were able to collaborate with an organisation of a global repute like the Bhavan. Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra Vice-Chairman Nalli Kuppuswami Chetti, Secretary M. Murali, and Director K.N. Ramaswamy were among those who spoke at the event. fca58b12f1386646.title: IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30
fca58b12f1386646.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:19 am IST - CHENNAI A 16-member delegation from Osaka took part in the business networking meeting held by the Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Chennai on Friday. | Photo Credit: RAGU R. The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan. The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka. The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities. To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4. The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka. “We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan. “India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added. He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation. a3d95c5cf6358b76.title: Same soil, different bowls: How dals sustained Dalit kitchens through scarcity
a3d95c5cf6358b76.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 06:00 am IST Shahu Patole, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada ( Anna He Apoorna Brahma. ). | Photo Credit: Special arrangement When Shahu Patole was growing up in Khamgaon village, in Osmanabad taluka in Maharashtra, in the 1960s, he remembers stories of how toor dal was difficult to come by. The food crisis in the mid-1960s, triggered by two successive droughts, had made pulses scarce and expensive. Toor dal production, for instance, fell from 1.89 million tonnes to 1.13 million tonnes between 1964 and 1967, according to government data. So, traders would sell lakh dal (grass pea; Lathyrus sativus) instead of toor , which was a long-duration crop that took more than six months to mature, or adulterate toor with the cheaper, drought-resistant legume. This was despite the Indian government prohibiting the sale of lakh dal in 1961, because the slightly bitter-tasting dal was dangerous for health. It caused lathyrism, an irreversible neurological and skeletal condition (many people suffered from paralysis of the lower limbs). The fact that such dangerous alternatives continued to be consumed in certain States, shows how essential people considered dals to be. “When meat wasn’t available, we relied on dals ,” says Patole, 63, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada (2024), adding that today toor , mung , chana , masur , urad , matki , chavli , and watane are the staples. In his village, there has been a long-standing practice of paying agricultural labourers their harvest produce in lieu of majdoori (daily wages). “If our household women harvested mung , they would be given akkha mung ki phali [whole mung stems]. 0682d324144b9209.title: Blue-green infrastructure, heat-risk modelling considered for Chennai’s Third Master Plan
0682d324144b9209.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - Chennai Integrating greenhouse gas emissions reductions, heat adaptation and flood mitigation into statutory planning, zoning regulations and master plans was discussed at the Conference on Climate Responsive Urban Planning in Chennai on Friday. The event detailed how heat-risk modelling, hydrological vulnerability assessments, and blue-green infrastructure strategies from three years of collaboration with the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) are shaping statutory policies for Chennai’s Third Master Plan (2026-2046), according to a press release. Two 60-minute technical sessions covered integrating climate actions into urban planning and localising climate action. They included discussion on bridging Climate Action Plans with day-to-day spatial planning, and a presentation on the Madhavaram Local Area Plan. Marking 10 years of Chennai’s C40 Cities membership, the conference launched the Climate Action Guide for Urban Planners in India, following the 2024 Cairo global guide. The Clean Air Zones Report, Urban Planning Accelerator signing, and Chennai’s entry into Youth Reinventing Cities for a Tiruvottiyur neighbourhood were also announced. The Jameel C40 Urban Planning Climate Labs with the CMDA and the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) convened the event. More than 75 exhibitors from over 10 States and five international destinations are taking part. Rajasthan Tourism and Delhi Tourism are the partner States. Andhra Pradesh Tourism is showcasing the State’s beaches, heritage sites, pilgrim centres and nature tourism. The stalls cover hotels, resorts, airlines, cruises and travel technology. The expo is open to the travel trade and the public. “Visakhapatnam is an important and growing travel market, and we are delighted to bring this platform to the city,” said Rohit Hangal, Director, Sphere Travelmedia and Exhibitions Pvt. Ltd. Tours and Travels Association of Andhra Pradesh president K. Vijaymohan, Hotel and Restaurant Association of Andhra Pradesh president Pavan Kartheek and officials of the Rajasthan, Delhi and Andhra Pradesh tourism departments attended the inauguration. The expo ends on Saturday. The next edition will be held in Coimbatore on January 29 and 30, 2027. 9b05f1cbd283c534.title: World Bank to assist CAG in urban governance audit for 101 Indian cities
9b05f1cbd283c534.summary: New Delhi: The World bank will assist India's Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) in examining how 101 Indian cities manage their finances, build infrastructure and deliver essential public services, as growing urban needs put pressure on municipal resources. The multilateral agency will provide technical expertise and international best practices to support the audit. The CAG is conducting a multi-year audit of urban infrastructure and services, starting with urban mobility, to provide a comprehensive assessment of municipal governance, finances and service delivery. The exercise will subsequently cover water and sanitation, housing, air quality management and liveable urban environments, with a different theme taken up each year, the comptroller and auditor general K. Sanjay Murthy said on Friday. The World Bank initiative, 'Strengthening Audit Capacity and Governance Accountability in India's Urban Sector', has been endorsed by the department of economic affairs. The exercise comes against the backdrop of growing need to strengthen municipal finances through better revenue mobilization, improved cost recovery and innovative financing mechanisms that are critical for cities to meet growing infrastructure and service delivery needs. The Union budget for 2026-27 also underscored government's focus on urban infrastructure development and the need to boost finance streams of urban local bodies, particularly for their ability to diversify revenue sources, improve financial sustainability and mobilize resources for expanding civic infrastructure. Speaking at a two-day workshop on urban infrastructure financing and municipal finance in New Delhi, Murthy said the audit of 101 cities would provide a holistic and comparable assessment of how cities are performing. He called for a sectoral approach to auditing so that multiple aspects of urban development could be assessed together. ec1b997eca2300f5.title: Indian dream has a Thai address
ec1b997eca2300f5.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:17 am IST Among overseas property destinations for Indian buyers, Dubai used to be the most popular and often go-to choice. However, with Thailand and its relatively accessible prices, tourism-led rental demand and holiday home appeal, Phuket, particularly, is drawing Indian buyers. According to Stuart Reading, managing director, Group Property Development at Banyan Group, “Indians are the fifth-largest buyers by value for Laguna Phuket, and they are the second-largest group of tourists in Phuket.” Banyan Group runs Laguna Phuket, a 1,000-acre integrated resort at Bang Tao with six hotels, a golf course and more than 3,000 branded residences. He says that Thailand drew over 35 million visitors in 2025, and foreign buyers account for over 60% of Phuket’s condominium purchases. “The core buyer is a high-net-worth individual or family office purchasing a legacy or trophy asset rather than a first home. It is often a second or third property bought for long-term capital preservation as much as lifestyle. We’re also seeing more second-home buyers relocating seasonally or working remotely from Phuket,” adds Reading. According to Shiv Garg, director of Forteasia Realty Pvt. Ltd, a Delhi-based real estate developer, Thailand, particularly Phuket, is gaining traction as an alternative option rather than as a direct substitute for Dubai, largely due to its relatively lower property prices. Phuket is also perceived to offer greater capital appreciation potential. 2592b7889ee0f9b9.title: Metrowater MD reviews work to resume production at Minjur desalination plant
2592b7889ee0f9b9.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:14 am IST - CHENNAI Chennai Metrowater has stepped up efforts to resume drinking water production at the 100 million litres a day plant. | Photo Credit: R_Shivaji Rao Chennai Metrowater has stepped up efforts to resume drinking water production at the 100 million litres a day (mld) Minjur desalination plant, with the first phase aimed at restoring its 20 mld capacity. Metrowater’s Managing Director T. Anand reviewed the ongoing works on Friday and directed the officials to submit weekly progress reports. A press release said he reviewed the work to remove accumulated sediment from the seawater intake sump and clean it using the jet wash method. He also reviewed works to restore the membranes in the seawater reverse osmosis section, which is a key component of the desalination process. Mr. Anand also enquired about the measures being taken to strengthen the plant’s automation and instrumentation systems, and progress of the detailed project report being prepared by the Tamil Nadu Water Investment Company. a093184977a9a8bb.title: Ensure no household is left out in Census enumeration, officials told
a093184977a9a8bb.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:26 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM District Revenue Officer S.D. Anita on Friday directed officials to complete the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 accurately and within the stipulated time. Addressing a two-day training programme for district and charge-level officers at the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) South Zone office at Suryabagh, she said that because the city is densely populated, officials should make sure no household is missed. Homeless people must also be counted, she added. Ms. Anita said self-enumeration would be open to residents from January 10 to 24, 2027. The technical glitches in the app during the housing listing phase had been fixed, she said, and officials should make the public aware of the facility. She pointed out that citizens are legally required to provide information under the Census Act, 1948. GVMC Additional Commissioner K. Ramesh suggested a target of at least 40% self-enumeration to reduce the burden on field staff. Census Joint Director S. Dayasagar also spoke. c06a14ccdd7f3879.title: Court rejects anticipatory bail pleas of six in Siddaramaiah ‘sting’ case
c06a14ccdd7f3879.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:49 am IST - Bengaluru A Bengaluru court on Friday rejected the anticipatory bail applications of six people, including expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, media coodinator to Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy, in connection with the alleged sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Another suspect in the case Power TV owner and editor Rakesh Shetty has also filed a separate anticipatory bail plea that is still pending, sources said. The applications were filed by six people, including Kripa Alva, Prajwal Prasad, Chandan, Vinod Kumar, Prashanth, and one other person. The Bengaluru City Police had opposed the bail applications. The rejection of anticipatory bail pleas of the six accused in the case, may likely lead to their arrest and custodial interrogation, sources said. Bengaluru City Police had registered a case under the Information Technology Act, 2000 based on a complaint by Mr. Siddaramaiah of a video, allegedly being circulated to defame him. The probe into the contents of the video had led the police to the official residence of Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy. Former Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh had said that Ritesh Pandey who had uploaded the video online had got a mobile phone for the purpose at the Union Minister’s residence. Meanwhile, the city police had also questioned the woman in the video, reportedly making allegations of sexual abuse against the former chief minister and she has reportedly denied any abuse. She has reportedly claimed she made those statements under pressure. This has put Kripa Alva and Rakesh Shetty, allegedly in the video in a spot and are facing heat from the police. 3318e4b46085b06a.title: Gurugram court fines Burger King, Swiggy ₹72,000 over delivery of non-veg burgers instead of veg
3318e4b46085b06a.summary: Burger King India and food delivery platform Swiggy have been held liable by a consumer court for delivering non-vegetarian burgers instead of vegetarian ones, following which two children reportedly fell ill. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission imposed a combined penalty of ₹ 72,000 on the two companies in connection with the 2021 incident. According to the complaint, Bhagwan Das Mangla, a resident of Sector 46 in Gurugram, had ordered four vegetarian burgers from Burger King through the Swiggy app on April 2, 2021, for his unwell wife. However, as she was not feeling well enough to eat, she left the package unopened. The burgers were subsequently opened and consumed by her children. According to Mangala, they found the taste strange and experienced nausea and vomiting. He said when he checked the package in the evening, he realised the food was non-vegetarian, which prompted him to raise a complaint with Swiggy. "This incident hurt the religious sentiments of my vegetarian family, leaving them under mental distress. When they raised an objection, a Burger King representative acknowledged the error and proposed an out-of-court settlement. The company offered to sponsor a pilgrimage to one or two destinations of the family's choice, in addition to providing compensation of ₹ 25,000. I rejected this proposal and filed a case in the consumer court, seeking compensation of ₹ 60,000," Mangla said. According to his counsel Megha Gupta, the matter was heard by a bench comprising Commission Chairperson Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. The Commission stated that the invoices, Swiggy app chat history, and complaint-related documents submitted by the complainant are sufficient to establish negligence on the part of the companies. 2ab0bd08a06939ca.title: TNGCTA writes to CM, Higher Education Minister to appoint senior govt. college principal as DCE
2ab0bd08a06939ca.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:10 am IST - Chennai The Tamil Nadu Government College Teachers Association (TNGCTA) has submitted a petition to the Chief Minister, Higher Education Minister, and Higher Education Secretary requesting the appointment of a senior college principal as the Director of Collegiate Education. The Association urged the government to revert to the old practice that was prevalent before January 2024, when a the senior-most principal of a government college would occupy the post of Director of Collegiate Education (DCE). Putting forth its argument, the association stated that the responsibility of administering over a 1,000 government Arts and Science colleges, government colleges of education, government-aided colleges, and self-financing colleges in the State should be entrusted to a person with deep understanding of the inner workings of these institutions. S. Suresh, general secretary, TNGCTA, said in a statement that senior principals had extensive experience in administering several of these institutions, which had prompted the government to appoint them and run the department for about three decades. However, on January 30, 2024, the then DCE was placed under suspension on administrative grounds and an IAS officer was appointed to streamline the affairs at the Directorate. This appointment was to be for a period of one year but the government kept appointing IAS officers ever since. The petition was prompted by the fact that the current DCE has gone on long leave due to personal reasons and the Commissioner of Technical Education, another IAS officer, was given additional charge of DCE. While the Commissioner has to administer a large number of technical educational institutions, he is also the head of Vice-Chancellor Convenor Committees of at least two State-run universities. Saddled with all these responsibilities, the Commissioner would find it difficult to ensure smooth functioning of the Collegiate Education department, Mr. Suresh

4dfc64ac7349a59e.title: India's core sector growth hit 31-month high of 10.9% in October
4dfc64ac7349a59e.summary: Output of key infrastructure industries rose 10.9 per cent in October 2026, up from 0.8 per cent in the year-ago month, driven by strong performance in coal, iron ore, electricity and cement. According to the official data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry on Friday, the core sector expanded by 8.2 per cent in September 2026. Among segments, iron ore output rose by 26.4 per cent, electricity by 21.6 per cent, coal by 23.1 per cent, and cement by 15.4 per cent. During April-October this fiscal, these nine segments expanded by 6 per cent against 2.3 per cent in the same period last year.

1ac5415d69379357.title: Forum explores perspectives on equity-oriented social progress and health systems
1ac5415d69379357.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:07 am IST - CHENNAI Panellists discuss equity-oriented social development and health systems at the “Transdisciplinary Practice and Research Forum” in Alwarpet on Friday. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B. Bringing together researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and people with lived experiences, a ‘Transdisciplinary Practice and Research Forum’ provided a platform to discuss diverse perspectives and experiences in addressing equity-oriented social development and health systems. The Banyan Academy of Leadership in Mental Health (BALM), along with Athena Institute at Vrije Universiteit, Amsterdam, organised the forum as part of their collaborative work on transdisciplinary research and practice. It sought to explore how academic and societal knowledge could be integrated into equity-oriented social development and health systems and how to build a community of practice around it. A panel discussion on “Epistemic Justice and Politics of Knowledge” discussed the epistemic politics of knowledge production, what is rendered visible or authoritative, by whom, and against which criteria of validity. Namita Jacob of Chetana Trust spoke about their work on creating accessible books for children with disabilities. “We need to understand their way of knowing the world,” she said, adding that they also run a library that travels to places so that children can have access to books. The books, she said, were not based on their impairments, but the barriers they faced or their requirements. Kavitha Muralidharan, independent journalist, said, “We must create spaces for people to tell their stories, rather than assuming that we must speak for them.” Journalists, she said, need to be careful about the hierarchy they create. She also stressed the importance of oral history. Pradeep Narayanan of Praxis said research methodology tools must not imprison conversations. b94d9fe20128b287.title: Freshwater fish species discovered in Western Ghats
b94d9fe20128b287.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:17 am IST - KOCHI Researchers at Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) claimed to have discovered two new freshwater fish species from the Periyar-Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats. Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum, one of the two species, has been named after the Mannan community and is found in streams deep inside the Periyar Tiger Reserve. The second species, Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis, is named after the Sabari hills and is found in streams near Angamoozhi in the Pamba river system, according to a communication. The discoveries were made by a team led by V.K. Anoop and Rajeev Raghavan from the Kufos and Neelesh Dahanukar from the Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence, New Delhi. The research has been published in the Journal of Fish Biology , it said. e4b128486e1a1120.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
e4b128486e1a1120.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:20 am IST - HYDERABAD The Gandhi Hospital team with the woman and her triplets. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment. Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle. After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother. Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha. IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre. d5544a7f2b36e4c0.title: Singareni keen to supply Naini coal to NTPC Kaniha plant after meeting TG needs
d5544a7f2b36e4c0.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:54 am IST - HYDERABAD Singareni CMD Buddhaprakash Jyoti (third from left) and two senior executives of SCCL with NTPC CMD Gurdeep Singh (second from left) in New Delhi on Friday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) has agreed to supply coal from its Naini Block mines in Odisha to local industries and NTPC’s Kaniha (Talcher) Thermal Power Station in Angul district there after meeting the coal requirements of Telangana. Chairman and Managing Director of the SCCL Buddhaprakash Jyoti expressed the company’s readiness during a meeting with CMD of the National Thermal Power Corporation Ltd (NTPC) Gurdeep Singh in New Delhi on Friday. Executive Director (Coal Movement) B. Venkanna and General Manager (Coordination and Marketing) T. Srinivas of SCCL also attended the meeting. During the meeting, Dr. Jyothi briefed Mr. Singh on production at the Naini coal block. He stated that the coal requirements of Telangana are being given priority with a major share of Naini coal mined now being supplied to the TG-Genco’s Yadadri Thermal Power Station. The remaining coal is being supplied to local industries. He assured that SCCL was ready to supply coal to NTPC’s Kaniha plant in addition to its existing coal supply agreements with NTPC. Mr. Jyoti added that SCCL has been supplying coal to NTPC plants in Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka and other States for decades under the fuel supply agreements. After Telangana, NTPC plants receive the largest share of SCCL’s coal production. The SCCL CMD stated that the Naini coal block is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of coal annually from next year and the production is planned to continue for the next four decades. Accordingly, the SCCL is ready to supply coal to the nearby NTPC Kaniha plant under a long-term fuel supply agreement. The accused was identified as K Rakesh, a catering worker and resident of Sarada Nagar Colony, Anakapalli. According to the police, the accused Rakesh gained entry into a locked house in Sarada Nagar Colony. The owners, after returning home on November 19, found that the gold was stolen and lodged a complaint. The police used technical evidence to identify the suspect and apprehended the accused. Entire stolen gold of 40.590 grams was recovered Police said Rakesh was a habitual offender and had been previously arrested in three theft cases at Anakapalli Town, S. Rayavaram and Munagapaka police stations. The accused was subsequently produced before the court. The owners, after returning home on November 19, found that the gold was stolen and lodged a complaint. The police used technical evidence to identify the suspect and apprehended the accused. Entire stolen gold of 40.590 grams was recovered Police said Rakesh was a habitual offender and had been previously arrested in three theft cases at Anakapalli Town, S. Rayavaram and Munagapaka police stations. The accused was subsequently produced before the court. bd1e48fa31b9c29e.title: Andhra govt to explore SMR nuclear plants as alternative to thermal power
bd1e48fa31b9c29e.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government on Friday approved tapping nuclear power employing Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology, advanced nuclear reactors, as an alternative to thermal power, an official said. K Vijayanand, special chief secretary (Energy), said the southern state would explore setting up nuclear power plants using SMR technology at "retiring thermal power units or other suitable locations in the state after SMR technology is stabilised." "Government, after careful consideration of the request of the Managing Director, APGENCO (Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation), hereby accord approval to explore establishment of a Nuclear Power Plant using SMR technology, as an alternative to thermal power," Vijayanand said in a Government Order (GO). The special chief secretary noted that the private sector will be allowed to participate in Andhra Pradesh's endeavour to set up SMR nuclear power plants.

71f45d913f0e75c2.title: NYC Fitness Buffs Bristle at City Plan to Close Outdoor Gym
71f45d913f0e75c2.summary: (Bloomberg) -- In New York’s neighborhood-level disputes over government projects, even pull-up bars have become a flashpoint. At Tompkins Square Park in Manhattan, the paint on a set of bars is chipping. But the fitness buffs who work out in the park daily are holding on to them for dear life. At issue are city proposals to close the outdoor gym for months and replace it with equipment that is more accessible to people with disabilities. Regulars argue the equipment is sufficiently accessible and that the city could reconstruct it with inferior materials. Some simply dread a monthslong separation from the bars that have become part of their daily lives. For Theophilus London, the stakes feel particularly personal. About three months ago, when he was struggling and looking to change his life, he found his way to the pull-up bars in Tompkins Square Park. “I was in a desperate need of a change of lifestyle,” London said on a recent afternoon, between sets at the East Village park. “This park changed my life.” London, a musician nominated for a Grammy Award with Kanye West in 2016, visits the pull-up bars daily. He is among many park-goers speaking against plans to close the decades-old fitness equipment for renovations. The park adds to a list of government projects that some New Yorkers have perceived as community interference. A few blocks southwest, in Nolita, residents protested the construction of an affordable housing project at Elizabeth Street Garden for more than a decade. Across the East River in Brooklyn, plans to build a skate park at Mount Prospect Park concerned neighborhood groups that said the facility would exacerbate the problem of higher temperatures in urban areas. “The idea that it’s an adult fitness area that needs reconstruction is totally and completely misguided,” said Salo Coslovsky, an urban planning professor at New York University, at a recent local advisory board meeting on the Tompkins Square Park pull-up bars. 800d656f16ed2f2d.title: No suburban service cancelled in morning peak hours due to new timetable: Railways
800d656f16ed2f2d.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:10 am IST - Chennai The Southern Railway has denied that there has been a reduction of suburban train services because of the new timetable that came into effect from November 1. In response to an article published in The Hindu, titled ‘Commuters from Pattabiram hit by reduced suburban services after revision of timetable’ on November 19, the Southern Railway has clarified that no suburban train services have been cancelled or withdrawn during the morning peak hours. Instead, the existing pattern of train operations has been strategically reorganised to improve overall operational efficiency, punctuality, and passenger convenience. With reference to the stoppage of the Pattabiram turnback service, which was extended to Tiruvallur, the Southern Railway says the turnback, introduced in 2004, involved a complex crossover movement, as the train had to cross over three lines to reach Pattabiram station, which is located on the line leading towards Pattabiram Military Siding. This crossover resulted in a speed restriction of 15 km per hour. The crossover movement consumed 10 to 12 minutes, causing the halting of trains on the three lines while approaching Pattabiram, leading to delays of mail and express trains as well. 224994778036cc8f.title: Cauvery dispute: SC dismisses Tamil Nadu's pleas for 11 TMC water release
224994778036cc8f.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed two pleas of the Tamil Nadu government seeking a direction to Karnataka for the release of 11 thousand million cubic (TMC) feet of Cauvery river water. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said that Tamil Nadu has filed a third application for bringing on record some additional documents, which will also be dismissed. In its pleas, the Tamil Nadu government sought directions to Karnataka to make sure that the backlog of 11 TMC of Cauvery water as on October 7 is cleared immediately and ensure the same at the rate of 1.3 TMC per day in 10 days at Billigundulu, a key water-measuring station on the banks of the river along the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border. On October 12, the top court reserved its decision on the two applications of the Tamil Nadu government. The Karnataka government had told the top court that it would be difficult to meet Tamil Nadu's demand for the release of 11 TMC feet of Cauvery river water for making good

a6d1195950f3317e.title: Two Tamil Nadu schools win inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards
a6d1195950f3317e.summary: Updated - November 20, 2026 01:08 am IST - CHENNAI Students of Kaligi Ranganathan Montford Matriculation Higher Secondary School with the inaugural Earthshot Challenge award. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Two schools in Tamil Nadu have won the inaugural I CAN Earthshot Challenge for developing solutions to environmental problems, ranging from plastic pollution to water conservation. Kaligi Ranganathan Montford Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Perambur, Chennai, won in the ‘Protect and Restore Nature’ category for its initiative, ‘Tiny Action, Mighty Impact’. A team of six students from Classes 7 and 8 took up the challenge of making their school more environmentally sustainable through four student-led initiatives focusing on carbon emissions, plastic waste, water conservation, and food waste. One of their interventions was collecting used milk packets from students of the school, which were washed, dried and handed over to Exnora International to be reused as grow bags for plants. “We collected more than 50,000 milk packets. Everyone supported us and brought them to school with interest,” said Janavi M., a Class 8 student who was part of the team. They also began collecting water discharged by the school’s 63 air-conditioners for reuse in cleaning corridors and restrooms and watering plants. S. Enitha said to reduce the carbon footprint of the school, the team encouraged parents to opt for walking or cycling for short commutes. “We learned to make seed balls and threw them in empty spaces around our school where nothing was growing,” she said. Teacher coordinator Gomathi said the team decided to take up four interconnected initiatives towards making the school carbon-neutral. “We cannot completely control carbon emissions, but we can take steps to reduce them and compensate by such small actions,” she said. The project was among 15 finalists selected from 974 submissions. The winners were announced at the Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony organised

4b9f2983919a6940.title: Reject rolls, use updated 2025 voter list for local polls, says anti-SIR Coalition
4b9f2983919a6940.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 06:01 am IST - Bengaluru The coalition has demanded that the government reject the SIR final rolls, conduct local body elections using the 2025 electoral rolls updated through the proposed social audit. | Photo Credit: File photo Rejecting the final electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Anti-SIR Coalition in Karnataka, pointing to the large-scale wrongful deletions and discrepancies, has requested the State government to conduct an independent social audit to identify eligible voters left out of the rolls. The coalition has demanded that the government reject the SIR final rolls, conduct local body elections using the 2025 electoral rolls updated through the proposed social audit, and take a clear stand on the issue amid uncertainty over which electoral rolls should be used for the upcoming local body polls. Recently, the State Election Commission directed that the SIR final rolls will be used as a base for GBA elections, slated to be held before December 31. However, the Congress-led State government, which has been opposing the exercise, has not announced a clear stand yet, though the issue was discussed in the cabinet. In a statement on Thursday, the coalition announced a State-wide investigation campaign from November 20 to December 20 to document cases of wrongful deletion, exclusion of eligible voters and procedural irregularities in the SIR process. Booth-level public hearings will be held at several locations across the State on December 20, it said. The coalition said Karnataka had an estimated adult population of 5.2 crore, while the final electoral rolls contained only around 4.5 crore names, leaving nearly 70 lakh people unaccounted for. It questioned how such a large gap could remain despite the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) stated objective of ensuring that no eligible voter was left out. 9b051c1130e81e0a.title: Nashik Court grants bail to Imtiaz Jaleel in TCS case on ₹50,000 bond
9b051c1130e81e0a.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 04:08 am IST AIMIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel. File. | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Nashik District and Sessions Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) granted bail to AIMIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel, a co-accused in the TCS conversion and harassment case, after he appeared before the court and submitted a bond of ₹50,000, following the prosecution’s opposition to his plea. When Mr. Jaleel appeared before the court to file the application for bail, the counsel representing the state opposed the plea, but the court approved the release upon the submission of the bond because the sections invoked against him permit release on bail. The investigation into the TCS case established that Nida Khan evaded law enforcement for two months by staying in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. During the probe into the shelter provided to Khan, officials questioned MIM corporator Matin Patel to determine who directed him. The retrieval of evidence from devices and items led the police to name Jaleel, Patel, and individuals associated with them as co-accused in the case for providing assistance to a person evading law enforcement. ff2134de32bccce3.title: ‘Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted’: PM Modi's blunt message to India Inc at FICCI AGM | 10 key takeaways
ff2134de32bccce3.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday, November 19, urged Indian businesses to move beyond the domestic market, improve product quality, reduce import dependence and expand their global footprint, calling on industry leaders to make India First the foundation of their long-term investment decisions. Addressing the 100th Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, PM Modi outlined opportunities across the pharmaceuticals, agriculture, food processing, engineering, steel and aluminium sectors. He also challenged businesses to translate the benefits of tax reforms into higher salaries and more employment, while invoking Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance. Here are the key takeaways from PM Modi's address: PM Modi urged businesses to stop treating India's large domestic market as an assured destination for products, stressing that Indian consumers deserve the same quality of goods as overseas buyers. He criticised the practice of selling products to Indian customers by describing them as "export quality". "Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted as an assured market where anything will sell. Even today, sellers tell customers 'this is export quality' to convince them it is good. What do you take our countrymen for? Do they not deserve good quality? This mindset must change; my countrymen deserve top quality," he said. He added that India's domestic market should serve as a launchpad for global competitiveness rather than become a comfort zone. "Our domestic market must not become our comfort zone. It should give us the confidence to compete in global markets," PM Modi said. The Prime Minister asked industry leaders to look beyond short-term business gains and prepare for emerging requirements in India and international markets. He called on businesses to prioritise national interests while making long-term investment decisions over the next tw

The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court. “Work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited. An additional district court should also be set up in the court complex”, said A.C. Devakumar, president, Bar Association (Vaniyambadi). At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town. Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court. It has resulted in hardship for litigants, advocates, and court staff to commute from one court to another as some petitioners have cases in different courts that will be taken up on the same day. The Judicial Magistrate Court, the oldest among three courts, was located in the Government Estate since the 1920s. The District Munsif court, formed in 1995, was functioning from a rented room in the Government Commercial Tax building. The subordinate court that was created in 2009 was also operating from a rented room in the town. Every day, on an average, more than 150 litigants, mostly from Vaniyambadi taluk that comprises 45 villages, visit these courts. Around 75 advocates are working as regular practitioners. On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day. Currently, 1,500 - 2,000 cases are pending before each of these three courts. Case bundles and court records get damaged during monsoon as the building is inundated. The court also does not have an audio system, to call for cases or parties. 33a189cc4e600e4a.title: A hundred years ago | Letter to Swedish academy
33a189cc4e600e4a.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 03:16 am IST London, Nov. 19: Mr. Bernard Shaw tenders his best thanks for the award (Nobel Prize) but says that his readers and audiences provide more than sufficient money for his needs and that his renown is greater than is good for his spiritual health. The money therefore to him is like a lifebelt thrown to a swimmer who has already safely reached the shore. He proceeds to point out some very advantageous sites in London which are being rapidly filled by agencies in which not only the Dominions but also the European powers exhibit very choice products to advertise travel attractions and all sorts of things to tempt the importer but a book is rarely exhibited. Sweden invites us to buy paper, but nothing is printed on it. The function of the Swedish paper seems to be to wrap up Australian apples. Sweden’s most valuable export is her literature of which Britons are deplorably ignorant. He suggests that the money accompanying the award should be funded and the proceeds annually used to encourage understanding in literature and art between Sweden and British Isles. especially the translations of valuable Swedish books. a7145ea5fe74af02.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 01:03 am IST - KOCHI A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board. The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions. It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster. The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board. The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S. Hamza and member C.K. Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution. The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge. The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members. f3313cea8f44a530.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 03:47 am IST Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the CBI, submitted that the issue may require deeper examination by the court. File. | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stayed proceedings before the Lokpal against Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in connection with a corruption complaint concerning promotions at the National Productivity Council (NPC). A Bench of Justice Subramonium Prasad and Justice Renu Bhatnagar sought responses from the Lokpal and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on a petition by Mr. Singh challenging the Lokpal’s March 4, 2025, and October 26, 2026, orders and the October 28 notice directing him to appear for proceedings under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act. The court listed the matter for further hearing on January 20 next year. The complaint alleges irregularities and corruption in recruitment and promotions at the NPC. The allegations against Mr. Singh relate to his decision to forward an advisory committee report concerning the promotions to the NPC’s Governing Body for appropriate action, instead of directing the organisation to act on the report. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the CBI, submitted that the issue may require deeper examination by the court. He said the Lokpal directed a hearing against the petitioner for the second time “without crossing the threshold” laid down by the High Court in its November 28, 2025, judgment in the same case. 273a0be60a1b55a7.title: BIS officials raid packaged drinking water unit for unauthorised use of ISI mark
273a0be60a1b55a7.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 12:58 am IST - CHENNAI A team of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) officials seized packaged drinking water containers and labels at Ayappakkam for unauthorised use of the ISI mark during a raid conducted on Wednesday. A press release said 113 20-litre filled water containers and 103 empty containers, and about 1,600 labels were seized for bearing unauthorised BIS mark without valid licence. The raid was conducted at Time Packaged Drinking Water on Thiruverkadu Road in Ayappakkam. S.D. Dayanand, Senior Director and Head, BIS Chennai Branch Office, said the BIS certification was not mandatory for packaged drinking water under the present regulatory framework. However, any manufacturer or business establishment choosing to use the BIS Standard Mark on its products must hold a valid BIS licence, and ensure that the marking is used strictly in accordance with the conditions of the licence. 7487b59f62562d78.title: Delhi-NCR sees 25% growth in retail space leasing in Jan-Sep: JLL
7487b59f62562d78.summary: Leasing of retail spaces in shopping malls and high streets in Delhi-NCR rose 25 per cent to 2.47 million sq ft during the first nine months of this year on better demand from retailers, according to JLL. Real estate consultant JLL India said that the gross leasing of retail space across seven major cities increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to 9.36 million sq ft during January-September 2026 from 8.86 million sq ft in the year-ago period. Delhi-NCR emerged as the leading market for nine-month gross leasing, accounting for a 26 per cent share, followed closely by Mumbai (25 per cent) and Bengaluru (21 per cent). The consultant said that the total gross leasing in 2026 would surpass the 12.5 million sq ft recorded in 2025, supported by continued demand from both international and domestic retailers. 28cc680cd32ebf8f.title: Centre proposes separate licensing norms for wholesale trade of bulk drugs
28cc680cd32ebf8f.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed a separate licensing framework for the wholesale trade of bulk drugs, including active and inactive bulk substances, to strengthen regulatory oversight and accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain. The proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, seek to introduce separate application (19-BC) and licence (20-BC) forms for the wholesale of bulk drugs, distinct from the existing licensing provisions for formulations. At present, a common licence covers the wholesale of both formulations and bulk drugs. The proposed amendment seeks to establish a dedicated licensing framework for bulk drugs, enabling more focused regulatory oversight of their wholesale trade and greater accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain, the ministry said in a statement. 53ebce943f76d307.title: GTA 6 developers worry about layoffs despite working on Rockstar's ‘biggest’ game: ‘We have had no indication’
53ebce943f76d307.summary: Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) , a title expected to generate massive revenue. However, while the launch has sparked excitement among gamers, concerns about job security continue to trouble some of the developers behind the blockbuster game. In an article for The Guardian, Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar Games, highlighted the uncertainty surrounding employment in the gaming industry. He pointed out that contributing to one of the world's biggest video game releases does not necessarily protect developers from potential job cuts, particularly as studios continue to reduce their workforces. "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but It’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte said that working on a major game does not guarantee job security. He pointed to widespread job cuts across the gaming industry in recent years. Uriarte said employees had received no indication that layoffs were coming. He added that uncertainty across the gaming industry still made it hard not to worry about the future. Rockstar North employees are voting on whether to secure union recognition. If approved, the union could represent more than 1,600 employees. Uriarte said AI is changing how gaming studios work and raising questions about the future relevance of developers’ skills. He noted that gaming companies worldwide have eliminated thousands of positions in recent years, with an estimated 24,000 jobs disappearing over the past two years. The scale of these cuts, he said, has left even employees working on highly successful projects concerned about their professional future. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off," he added. The growing concerns over job security have also prompted employees at Rockstar North to consider collective action. Workers

598a429bcc296620.title: Devotees visiting Guruvayur temple must be treated with respect, says Kerala High Court
598a429bcc296620.summary: Published - November 20, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI The Kerala High Court has held that every devotee visiting the Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple ought to be cared for and treated with respect. Temple employees at every level must act with the highest degree of equanimity and must not lose their temper with any devotee. Every devotee would like to spend as much time as possible in front of the deity, and employees must ensure that the queue moves, with hundreds of others waiting for darshan. It thus requires a fine balance between rival interests. Whatever be the reason or provocation, an altercation or bad behaviour on the part of any employee cannot be tolerated, the High Court said. The standing counsel for the Guruvayur Devaswom Board intervened to say that there were instances when some devotees unfairly created provocation, leading, in one case, to a stabbing incident. Undoubtedly, the responsibility and obligation of civility is mutual. But if heated situations are not properly managed, things may spiral out of control, which will be deleterious to the pious and sanctified atmosphere of the temple, the court held, while closing two suo motu petitions based on complaints from devotees who alleged harassment by Devaswom staff. ab094a789e27cc17.title: Ananya Birla gets a ₹50,000 ‘Made in India’ luxury watch from Farah Khan: All about the Jaipur Watch Company piece
ab094a789e27cc17.summary: Ananya Birla, entrepreneur and singer, opened the doors of her family's Mumbai residence—the historic Jatia House bought by industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla for ₹ 425 crore in 2018—to filmmaker Farah Khan for a new episode of her vlog ‘Food With Farah’. While the grandeur of the mansion left the director visibly impressed, a rather unique timepiece that Khan brought as a present ended up taking centre stage during the visit. Presenting the horological piece by the homegrown brand Jaipur Watch Company to Birla, Khan said, “We got you this special gift from Jaipur,” revealing that the watch was specially picked from the brand's 'Gates of India' collection. Birla, admiring the present, said, “What I love is that it is made in India.” The Main Hoon Na director also highlighted that Indian brands are now crafting one-of-a-kind luxury pieces, and pointed out, “This is a Jaipur Gate.” She also revealed that the watch has a unique reversible feature: the bezel reveals Mumbai's iconic Gateway of India on the other side. Jaipur Watch Company, a homegrown luxury watch company, said its Gates of India – Gateway of India - LOTUS embraces the heart of Jaipur's City Palace's most celebrated entrances, the Lotus Gate/the Leheriya Gate of Pritam Niwas Chowk. “More than architectural masterpieces, these gateways symbolise prosperity, renewal, and the changing seasons, welcoming generations into the royal world of art, culture, and tradition,” the company said about its yet-to-be-released product. The watchmaker, however, said that the ₹ 50,000 watch Farah Khan gifted Ananya Birla can be pre-ordered and would take upto 75 days to process. The watch, Jaipur Watch Company said, is inspired by these iconic palace gates, reimagined as a passage through India's remarkable heritage. It features a unique flip mechanism that reveals the heritage landmark of Mumbai — the Gateway of India. 063e61ccc70ec880.title: Gold imports may fall to $40 bn in FY27 on duty hike: Commerce Secy
063e61ccc70ec880.summary: India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year. This has also helped manage the trade deficit, he said. In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports. India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25. Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. "I think... this year we will end up with USD 35-40 billion of gold imports. I think that is manageable in the current year... The current duty structure has a positive impact on the gold import," .

The two companies will undertake joint Front-End Engineering and Design (FEED) studies to support a Final Investment Decision (FID) by Tata Steel's board on the proposed project, it added. The total apartments will be 1,056," said Mallanna Sasalu, CEO-South, Puravankara. When asked about the project cost, he said the company already owns the land. "The investment on pure construction will be around Rs 800 crore," he told PTI. The estimated revenue potential from this upcoming project is about Rs 2,000 crore, Sasalu said. Passenger vehicle sales across the country totalled 13.61 lakh units in the second quarter of fiscal 2026-27, the industry body said. Maharashtra accounted for 1,65,000 units, or 12.1 per cent of the total, followed by Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Two-wheelers, India's largest vehicle segment by volume, saw sales of 64.33 lakh units in the quarter. Uttar Pradesh led with 7,89,000 units, or 12.3 per cent of the total, ahead of Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Karnataka.
